speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific location of your knee pain and what activities brought it on. Did you notice any swelling, redness, or a popping sound at the time of injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; the mechanism of repetitive pivoting and twisting is highly suggestive of a meniscal tear or an ACL injury. Can you tell me exactly where the pain is located on the knee and if you felt or heard a "pop" when it started? Also, does the knee feel unstable or give way when you walk?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; pain medial to the patella combined with your volleyball activity raises suspicion for a Medial Collateral Ligament (MCL) sprain or a Medial Meniscal tear. Did the pain start immediately upon landing or twisting, and is there any visible swelling or warmth in that area? REQUEST TEST: Knee_Physical_Examination_MCL

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Tenderness over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella; negative for ligamentous instability tests; no visible swelling or erythema noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the exam results; since instability tests are negative and there is no swelling, I am less concerned about a major ligament tear. Given the specific tenderness over the medial tibia and your history of pivoting, was your pain sharp and immediate at the moment of injury, or did it develop more gradually? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Knee

speaker: Measurement
